author: scottfalconer
body:
The `optimizer` parameter in the `plan_route` function (a string indicating the chosen optimizer like "greedy2opt") was shadowing the imported `optimizer` module. This caused an AttributeError when `use_advanced_optimizer` was true, as the code attempted to call `optimizer.advanced_2opt_optimization` on the string variable.

This commit renames the `optimizer` string parameter within `plan_route` to `optimizer_name` and updates all its call sites within the `challenge_planner.py` file. This ensures that `optimizer` within the scope of `plan_route` correctly refers to the imported module, allowing the `advanced_2opt_optimization` method to be found and called correctly.

author: frontman-git
body:
fix [3732](https://github.com/preactjs/preact/issues/4732)

When hydrating a `<template>` element, Preact fails to reuse existing DOM nodes inside `template.content`.  
This is because `<template>` elements encapsulate their children within a `DocumentFragment`, but the `diff`/`hydrate` logic doesn't switch the context to `template.content`.

As a result, hydration skips the existing fragment content and instead appends new nodes — leading to duplicated content in the DOM.

author: dnewcomb
body:
There are many situations were void areas with high standard deviation edge values should not be modeled as flat in a filled elevation raster. This modification adds an input option , stddev_limit.  Any void areas with edge standard deviation values above this limit are removed in an initial filled elevation raster using  r.mapcalc . The resulting raster is passed to r.fillnulls with the default values with the exception of tension,which is hard coded to 150 and memory, which is hard coded to 4000 MB  .

It may be that a memory input option with a default of 4000 MB might be better.  The reason I chose a tension of 150 is that is works with minimal overshoots for the data set in the tutorial that is in progress.

body:
This PR implements a comprehensive search and filtering system that transforms the Todo app from a basic task manager into a powerful productivity tool capable of efficiently handling large datasets.

## 🎯 Features Implemented

### Advanced Search Capabilities
- **Text Search**: Fuzzy matching, regex support, and exact match with quotes
- **Smart Search Syntax**: 
  - `status:active` - Filter by task status
  - `created:>2024-01-01` - Date-based filtering
  - `"exact match"` - Precise text matching
- **Search Options**: Case sensitivity toggle, regex mode, fuzzy search
- **Real-time Results**: Instant search with relevance scoring and match highlighting

### Enhanced Filtering System
- **Date Range Filtering**: Filter by creation, update, or due dates
- **Status Filtering**: Seamlessly integrated with existing all/active/completed filters
- **Multiple Conditions**: Combine text search with date and status filters
- **Visual Feedback**: Active filter indicators and result statistics

### User Experience Improvements
- **Search History**: Automatic management of 10 most recent searches
- **Keyboard Shortcuts**: `Ctrl+F` to focus search, `Esc` to clear
- **Mobile Responsive**: Collapsible advanced options, touch-friendly interface
- **Accessibility**: Proper ARIA labels, keyboard navigation support
- **Performance**: Debounced input and optimized search algorithms

## 🏗️ Technical Implementation

### New Components
- `SearchBar`: Advanced search input with options panel and history
- `AdvancedFilter`: Date range filtering with expandable UI
- `useSearch`: Custom hook for search state management and logic
- `useDebounce`: Performance optimization for search input

### Core Utilities
- `searchUtils.ts`: Fuzzy search, query parsing, and highlighting functions
- Advanced search syntax parser supporting complex queries
- Efficient date comparison and text matching algorithms

### Enhanced TodoApp
- Integrated search and filtering with existing functionality
- Search result statistics and active filter management
- Expandable advanced search interface
- Score-based result ordering with visual indicators

## 📊 Test Coverage

- **62/65 tests passing** (95% success rate)
- **Search Utilities**: 21/21 comprehensive algorithm tests ✅
- **SearchBar Component**: 6/6 UI interaction tests ✅
- **AdvancedFilter Component**: 8/8 filtering tests ✅
- **TodoApp Integration**: 7/7 end-to-end tests ✅
- Remaining failures are pre-existing TodoInput issues unrelated to search

## 🎨 Code Quality

- Follows established TypeScript and React patterns
- Comprehensive JSDoc documentation with emoji annotations
- ESLint compliant with no warnings or errors
- Minimal changes to existing codebase - purely additive
- Proper error handling and edge case coverage

## 🚀 Usage Examples

```typescript
// Basic text search
"meeting preparation"

// Advanced syntax
status:active created:>2024-01-01 "important task"

// Exact match
"complete project documentation"

// Date filtering
created:>=2024-01-01 created:<=2024-12-31
```

The search system provides immediate value for users managing large task lists while maintaining the simplicity of the original Todo app interface.

body:
# Comprehensive Deparser Improvements for PostgreSQL 13→17 Upgrade

This PR implements significant improvements to the pgsql-parser-v2 deparser functionality, focusing on upgrading compatibility from PostgreSQL 13 to PostgreSQL 17 and resolving critical parsing issues in the kitchen-sink tests.

## Key Improvements

### Window Function Handling
- **Fixed SQL clause ordering**: Moved `WINDOW` clause to come before `ORDER BY` clause in SelectStmt to match PostgreSQL syntax requirements
- **Added named window reference support**: Implemented proper handling of `OVER w` references with corresponding `WINDOW w AS (...)` definitions
- **Fixed empty window definitions**: Added support for `WINDOW w AS ()` syntax by ensuring `AS ()` is always added for named windows, even when empty
- **Enhanced WindowDef method**: Added explicit `AS` keyword handling for proper window definition syntax

### SubLink and Subquery Support
- **Implemented comprehensive SubLink deparser**: Added support for EXISTS, IN, NOT IN, ANY, ALL, and other subquery types
- **Fixed subquery expression handling**: Proper parenthesization and context management for nested queries
- **Enhanced A_Expr subquery support**: Improved handling of subqueries within expressions

### Multi-Column Assignment Support
- **Added MultiAssignRef detection**: Implemented proper handling for multi-column assignments in UPDATE statements
- **Enhanced assignment target processing**: Better support for complex assignment patterns

### DDL Statement Improvements
- **Fixed AlterTableCmd ADD COLUMN**: Resolved issues with generated column specifications
- **Enhanced CompositeTypeStmt**: Improved handling of composite type definitions
- **Added ON CONFLICT WHERE clause support**: Proper handling of conditional conflict resolution
- **Improved CreateTableAsStmt**: Added TEMPORARY keyword support and better table creation handling

### Expression and Function Enhancements
- **Enhanced NamedArgExpr**: Better handling of named function arguments
- **Improved DropStmt**: Enhanced object dropping with proper cascading and restriction handling
- **Fixed window frame specifications**: Better handling of frame options in window functions

## Test Progress

The changes have significantly improved the kitchen-sink test results:
- **Moved from syntax errors to AST mismatch errors**: This indicates the deparser is now generating valid SQL that parses correctly
- **Window function tests now pass**: Multiple window function test cases that previously failed with syntax errors now generate correct SQL
- **Reduced critical parsing failures**: Many node types that were previously unimplemented now have proper deparser support

## Technical Details

### Architecture
- Follows the existing visitor pattern in the Deparser class
- Maintains compatibility with existing utility classes (SqlFormatter, QuoteUtils, ListUtils)
- Preserves the parse → deparse → reparse cycle validation approach

### Code Quality
- Added comprehensive error handling and context propagation
- Maintained consistent naming conventions and patterns
- Ensured proper TypeScript typing throughout

## Testing

The changes have been tested against the comprehensive kitchen-sink test suite, which validates the parse → deparse → reparse cycle for hundreds of PostgreSQL SQL examples from upstream PostgreSQL test cases.

## 🚀 이슈 번호

**Resolve:** {#1264}

## 🧩 문제 해결

**스스로 해결:** ❌

### 🔎 접근 과정

> 문제 해결을 위한 접근 방식을 설명해주세요.

- 🔹 **어떤 알고리즘을 사용했는지** `구현`, `정렬`
- 🔹 **어떤 방식으로 접근했는지**
    - `x` 좌표를 딕셔너리의 키로 사용하고, 해당 `x`에서 가능한 `y` 좌표들을 리스트에 저장하여 `cafes`라는 딕셔너리 형태로 좌표를 구성했습니다.
    - 항상 `x` 좌표가 증가하는 방향으로 이동하며, 같은 `x`에서 `y` 좌표는 오르거나 내리는 방식으로 결정되기 때문에 정렬 방향을 동적으로 설정해야 합니다
    - 이전 좌표의 `y` 값과 현재 `x`의 가장 작은 `y` 값이 다를 경우, 이동 방향(정렬 방향)을 반전시켜야 합니다. 이를 통해 전체 좌표 순서를 정확히 결정하고, `ans` 배열에 순서대로 누적합니다.
    - 초반에는 우선순위 큐를 활용한 방법으로 접근했으나, `y`의 정렬 방향을 유연하게 다루기 위해 단일 딕셔너리 기반 정렬 방식으로 전환했습니다. `y` 값에 대해 오름차순/내림차순 큐를 별도로 두는 방식으로도 풀이 가능할 것으로 보입니다.

### ⏱️ 시간 복잡도

> **시간 복잡도 분석을 작성해주세요.**  
> 최악의 경우 수행 시간은 어느 정도인지 분석합니다.

- **Big-O 표기법:** `O(N^2)`
- **이유:**

## 💻 구현 코드

```Python
from collections import defaultdict

def solve(cafes, m):
    ans = [(0, 0)]
    for i in range(len(cafes)):
        cafes[i][1].sort()
        if ans[-1][1] != cafes[i][1][0]:
            cafes[i][1].sort(reverse = True)
        ans += [(cafes[i][0], j) for j in cafes[i][1]]

    for idx in m:
        print(*ans[idx])

T = int(input())
for _ in range(T):
    # Input
    n = int(input())
    cafes = defaultdict(list)
    for _ in range(n):
        x, y = map(int, input().split())
        cafes[x].append(y)
    m = list(map(int, input().split()))
    # Solve
    solve(sorted(cafes.items()), m[1:])
```

author: timosaarinen
body:
The `wait_for_agents` tool was incorrectly documented, promising a dictionary result within the same turn. This caused the LLM to generate code that immediately tried to process a return value, resulting in a `TypeError` because the tool actually returns a string directive for the main loop.



This commit fixes the issue by:

1.  Updating the `outputSchema` and `description` for `wait_for_agents` in `internal/agent_tools.py` to accurately reflect that it returns a directive string and that results are only available in the next turn.

2.  Rewriting the `AGENT ORCHESTRATION` guide in `prompts/system.txt` with a clear, two-turn example that demonstrates the correct spawn-wait-process workflow.



This ensures the LLM has an accurate understanding of the tool's behavior, preventing it from generating faulty code.

author: pedramamini
body:
**Summary**

Implements comprehensive MCP specification version detection to address issue #2. Now MCPeek can identify and display what MCP spec version a server supports during discovery operations.

**Key Features:**
- MCP version detection based on server capabilities and protocol version
- Version compatibility assessment with confidence scoring
- Support for multiple MCP specification versions (1.0.0, 0.9.0, 0.8.0)
- Enhanced discovery output with version information display
- Feature-based version inference for unknown protocol versions

**Test Plan:**
- [ ] Test discovery with various MCP servers (HTTP and STDIO)
- [ ] Verify version detection accuracy with known server versions
- [ ] Test compatibility assessment and confidence scoring
- [ ] Validate output formatting in both table and JSON modes
- [ ] Run existing test suite to ensure no regressions

Resolves #2

body:
This change sandboxes the creation of [`java.net.URL`](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/net/URL.html) objects so they will be more resistant to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks.

Most of the time when you create a URL, you're intending to reference an HTTP endpoint, like an internal microservice. However, URLs can point to local file system files, a Gopher stream in your local network, a JAR file on a remote Internet site, and all kinds of other unexpected and undesirable stuff. When the URL values are influenced by attackers, they can trick your application into fetching internal resources, running malicious code, or otherwise harming the system. Consider the following code:

```java
String url = userInput.getServiceAddress();
return IOUtils.toString(new URL(url).openConnection());
```

In this case, an attacker could supply a value like `jar:file:/path/to/appserver/lib.jar` and attempt to read the contents of your application's code.

Our changes introduce sandboxing around URL creation that force the developers to specify some boundaries on the types of URLs they expect to create:

```diff
+ import io.github.pixee.security.Urls;
+ import io.github.pixee.security.HostValidator;
  ...
  String url = userInput.getServiceAddress();
- URL u = new URL(url);
+ URL u = Urls.create(url, Urls.HTTP_PROTOCOLS, HostValidator.DENY_COMMON_INFRASTRUCTURE_TARGETS);
  InputStream is = u.openConnection();
```

This change alone reduces attack surface significantly, but can be enhanced to create even more security by specifying some controls around the hosts we expect to connect with:

```diff
+ import io.github.pixee.security.Urls;
+ import io.github.pixee.security.HostValidator;
  ...
  HostValidator allowsOnlyGoodDotCom = HostValidator.fromAllowedHostPattern(Pattern.compile("good\\.com"));
  URL u = Urls.create(url, Urls.HTTP_PROTOCOLS, allowsOnlyGoodDotCom);
```

Note: Beware temptation to write some validation on your own. Parsing URLs is difficult and differences between parsers in validation and execution will certainly lead to exploits as attackers [have repeatedly proven](https://www.blackhat.com/docs/us-17/thursday/us-17-Tsai-A-New-Era-Of-SSRF-Exploiting-URL-Parser-In-Trending-Programming-Languages.pdf).

author: pixeebot[bot]
body:
This codemod replaces all instances of functions in the `random` module (e.g. `random.random()` with their, much more secure, equivalents from the `secrets` module (e.g. `secrets.SystemRandom().random()`).

There is significant algorithmic complexity in getting computers to generate genuinely unguessable random bits. The `random.random()` function uses a method of pseudo-random number generation that unfortunately emits fairly predictable numbers.

If the numbers it emits are predictable, then it's obviously not safe to use in cryptographic operations, file name creation, token construction, password generation, and anything else that's related to security. In fact, it may affect security even if it's not directly obvious.

Switching to a more secure version is simple and the changes look something like this:

```diff
- import random
+ import secrets
  ...
- random.random()
+ secrets.SystemRandom().random()
```

author: pixeebot[bot]
body:
This codemod wraps assignments of `open` calls in a with statement. Without explicit closing, these resources will be "leaked" and won't be re-claimed until garbage collection. In situations where these resources are leaked rapidly (either through malicious repetitive action or unusually spiky usage), connection pool or file handle exhaustion will occur. These types of failures tend to be catastrophic, resulting in downtime and many times affect downstream applications.

Our changes look something like this:

```diff
import tempfile
path = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile().name
-file = open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8')
-file.write('Hello World')
+with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as file:
+   file.write('Hello World')
```

author: pixeebot[bot]
body:
This change updates all new instances of [ZipInputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/util/zip/ZipInputStream.html) to protect against malicious entries that attempt to escape their "file root" and overwrite other files on the running filesystem.

Normally, when you're using `ZipInputStream` it's because you're processing zip files. That code might look like this:

```java
File file = new File(unzipTargetDirectory, zipEntry.getName()); // use file name from zip entry
InputStream is = zip.getInputStream(zipEntry); // get the contents of the zip entry
IOUtils.copy(is, new FileOutputStream(file)); // write the contents to the provided file name
```

This looks fine when it encounters a normal zip entry within a zip file, looking something like this pseudo-data:
```binary
path: data/names.txt
contents: Zeus\nHelen\nLeda...
```

However, there's nothing to prevent an attacker from sending an evil entry in the zip that looks more like this:
```binary
path: ../../../../../etc/passwd
contents: root::0:0:root:/:/bin/sh
```

Yes, in the above code, which looks like [every](https://stackoverflow.com/a/23870468) [piece](https://stackoverflow.com/a/51285801) of [zip-processing](https://kodejava.org/how-do-i-decompress-a-zip-file-using-zipinputstream/)  code you can [find](https://www.tabnine.com/code/java/classes/java.util.zip.ZipInputStream) on the [Internet](https://www.baeldung.com/java-compress-and-uncompress), attackers could overwrite any files to which the application has access. This rule replaces the standard `ZipInputStream` with a hardened subclass which prevents access to entry paths that attempt to traverse directories above the current directory (which no normal zip file should ever do.) Our changes end up looking something like this:

```diff
+ import io.github.pixee.security.ZipSecurity;
  ...
- var zip = new ZipInputStream(is, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
+ var zip = ZipSecurity.createHardenedInputStream(is, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
```

author: pixeebot[bot]
body:
This codemod sandboxes calls to [`requests.get`](https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/#requests.get) to be more resistant to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks.

Most of the time when you make a `GET` request to a URL, you're intending to reference an HTTP endpoint, like an internal microservice. However, URLs can point to local file system files, a Gopher stream in your local network, a JAR file on a remote Internet site, and all kinds of other unexpected and undesirable outcomes. When the URL values are influenced by attackers, they can trick your application into fetching internal resources, running malicious code, or otherwise harming the system.
Consider the following code for a Flask app:

```python
from flask import Flask, request
import requests

app = Flask(__name__)

@app.route("/request-url")
def request_url():
    url = request.args["loc"]
    resp = requests.get(url)
    ...
```

In this case, an attacker could supply a value like `"http://169.254.169.254/user-data/"` and attempt to access user information.

Our changes introduce sandboxing around URL creation that force developers to specify some boundaries on the types of URLs they expect to create:

```diff
  from flask import Flask, request
- import requests
+ from security import safe_requests

  app = Flask(__name__)

  @app.route("/request-url")
  def request_url():
    url = request.args["loc"]
-   resp = requests.get(url)
+   resp = safe_requests.get(url)
    ...
```

This change alone reduces attack surface significantly because the default behavior of `safe_requests.get` raises a `SecurityException` if
a user attempts to access a known infrastructure location, unless specifically disabled.


If you have feedback on this codemod, [please let us know](mailto:feedback@pixee.ai)!

## F.A.Q. 

### Why does this codemod require a Pixee dependency?

We always prefer to use built-in Python functions or one from a well-known and trusted community dependency. However, we cannot find any such control. If you know of one, [please let us know](https://ask.pixee.ai/feedback).

### Why is this codemod marked as Merge After Cursory Review?

By default, the protection only weaves in 2 checks, which we believe will not cause any issues with the vast majority of code:
1. The given URL must be HTTP/HTTPS.
2. The given URL must not point to a "well-known infrastructure target", which includes things like AWS Metadata Service endpoints, and internal routers (e.g., 192.168.1.1) which are common targets of attacks.

However, on rare occasions an application may use a URL protocol like "file://" or "ftp://" in backend or middleware code.

If you want to allow those protocols, change the incoming PR to look more like this and get the best security possible:

```diff
-resp = requests.get(url)
+resp = safe_requests.get(url, allowed_protocols=("ftp",))
```

## Dependency Updates

This codemod relies on an external dependency. We have automatically added this dependency to your project's `requirements.txt` file. 

This library holds security tools for protecting Python API calls. 

There are a number of places where Python project dependencies can be expressed, including `setup.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`, and `requirements.txt` files. If this change is incorrect, or if you are using another packaging system such as `poetry`, it may be necessary for you to manually add the dependency to the proper location in your project.

author: pixeebot[bot]
body:
This change sandboxes the creation of [`java.net.URL`](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/net/URL.html) objects so they will be more resistant to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks.

Most of the time when you create a URL, you're intending to reference an HTTP endpoint, like an internal microservice. However, URLs can point to local file system files, a Gopher stream in your local network, a JAR file on a remote Internet site, and all kinds of other unexpected and undesirable stuff. When the URL values are influenced by attackers, they can trick your application into fetching internal resources, running malicious code, or otherwise harming the system. Consider the following code:

```java
String url = userInput.getServiceAddress();
return IOUtils.toString(new URL(url).openConnection());
```

In this case, an attacker could supply a value like `jar:file:/path/to/appserver/lib.jar` and attempt to read the contents of your application's code.

Our changes introduce sandboxing around URL creation that force the developers to specify some boundaries on the types of URLs they expect to create:

```diff
+ import io.github.pixee.security.Urls;
+ import io.github.pixee.security.HostValidator;
  ...
  String url = userInput.getServiceAddress();
- URL u = new URL(url);
+ URL u = Urls.create(url, Urls.HTTP_PROTOCOLS, HostValidator.DENY_COMMON_INFRASTRUCTURE_TARGETS);
  InputStream is = u.openConnection();
```

This change alone reduces attack surface significantly, but can be enhanced to create even more security by specifying some controls around the hosts we expect to connect with:

```diff
+ import io.github.pixee.security.Urls;
+ import io.github.pixee.security.HostValidator;
  ...
  HostValidator allowsOnlyGoodDotCom = HostValidator.fromAllowedHostPattern(Pattern.compile("good\\.com"));
  URL u = Urls.create(url, Urls.HTTP_PROTOCOLS, allowsOnlyGoodDotCom);
```

Note: Beware temptation to write some validation on your own. Parsing URLs is difficult and differences between parsers in validation and execution will certainly lead to exploits as attackers [have repeatedly proven](https://www.blackhat.com/docs/us-17/thursday/us-17-Tsai-A-New-Era-Of-SSRF-Exploiting-URL-Parser-In-Trending-Programming-Languages.pdf).

This PR add the basic configuration for deployments.

## Current Behavior

There is no automated deployment for this repository

## Expected Behavior

When a change is pushed to main branch this happens:

- A Docker image is build and pushed to AWS ECR
- An ECS Task Definition file is created using the secrets on this repository
- The ECS Task Definition is used to update the Service on the AWS ECS Cluster

- A Docker file was added
- An AWS folder is added and contains the Task Definition template and the script to fill the values
- A new workflow was added to automate the deployment

## Summary
- Implemented core static site generator with Markdown to HTML conversion
- Added EJS-based templating system with authentic 90s theme
- Created comprehensive test suite (unit, integration, E2E)

## Changes

### Core Features
- **Markdown Processing**: Full CommonMark support with syntax highlighting
- **Front Matter**: YAML metadata parsing for posts and pages
- **Template System**: EJS templates with base layout and page-specific templates
- **90s Theme**: Authentic retro styling with table-based layouts, web-safe colors, and period-appropriate CSS
- **Asset Management**: Automatic copying of static assets from content directory

### Technical Implementation
- Created `Generator` class in `src/generator.js` handling all build operations
- Updated CLI to execute actual builds instead of placeholder messages
- Added proper error handling and debug logging throughout
- Maintains source directory structure in output

### Testing
- **Unit Tests**: Test generator methods in isolation with mocks
- **Integration Tests**: Test full build process with real files
- **E2E Tests**: Test complete workflows from markdown to HTML

### Dependencies Added
- `markdown-it` - Markdown parser
- `gray-matter` - Front matter parser
- `ejs` - Template engine
- `fs-extra` - Enhanced file operations
- `jest` - Testing framework

## Test Plan
- [x] Run `npm test` - All tests pass
- [x] Run `retro-ssg build` - Generates static site in output directory
- [x] Verify generated HTML has proper 90s styling
- [x] Check that markdown features work (bold, links, code blocks)
- [x] Confirm assets are copied correctly
- [x] Test with various front matter configurations

# Build your 90s website
retro-ssg build

ls output/

This codemod will flip Django's `DEBUG` flag to `False` if it's `True` on the `settings.py` file within Django's default directory structure.

Having the debug flag on may result in sensitive information exposure. When an exception occurs while the `DEBUG` flag in on, it will dump metadata of your environment, including the settings module. The attacker can purposefully request a non-existing url to trigger an exception and gather information about your system.

```diff
- DEBUG = True
+ DEBUG = False
```

author: pixeebot[bot]
body:
This codemod sandboxes calls to [`requests.get`](https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/#requests.get) to be more resistant to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks.

Most of the time when you make a `GET` request to a URL, you're intending to reference an HTTP endpoint, like an internal microservice. However, URLs can point to local file system files, a Gopher stream in your local network, a JAR file on a remote Internet site, and all kinds of other unexpected and undesirable outcomes. When the URL values are influenced by attackers, they can trick your application into fetching internal resources, running malicious code, or otherwise harming the system.
Consider the following code for a Flask app:

```python
from flask import Flask, request
import requests

app = Flask(__name__)

@app.route("/request-url")
def request_url():
    url = request.args["loc"]
    resp = requests.get(url)
    ...
```

In this case, an attacker could supply a value like `"http://169.254.169.254/user-data/"` and attempt to access user information.

Our changes introduce sandboxing around URL creation that force developers to specify some boundaries on the types of URLs they expect to create:

```diff
  from flask import Flask, request
- import requests
+ from security import safe_requests

  app = Flask(__name__)

  @app.route("/request-url")
  def request_url():
    url = request.args["loc"]
-   resp = requests.get(url)
+   resp = safe_requests.get(url)
    ...
```

This change alone reduces attack surface significantly because the default behavior of `safe_requests.get` raises a `SecurityException` if
a user attempts to access a known infrastructure location, unless specifically disabled.


If you have feedback on this codemod, [please let us know](mailto:feedback@pixee.ai)!

## F.A.Q. 

### Why does this codemod require a Pixee dependency?

We always prefer to use built-in Python functions or one from a well-known and trusted community dependency. However, we cannot find any such control. If you know of one, [please let us know](https://ask.pixee.ai/feedback).

### Why is this codemod marked as Merge After Cursory Review?

By default, the protection only weaves in 2 checks, which we believe will not cause any issues with the vast majority of code:
1. The given URL must be HTTP/HTTPS.
2. The given URL must not point to a "well-known infrastructure target", which includes things like AWS Metadata Service endpoints, and internal routers (e.g., 192.168.1.1) which are common targets of attacks.

However, on rare occasions an application may use a URL protocol like "file://" or "ftp://" in backend or middleware code.

If you want to allow those protocols, change the incoming PR to look more like this and get the best security possible:

```diff
-resp = requests.get(url)
+resp = safe_requests.get(url, allowed_protocols=("ftp",))
```

## Dependency Updates

This codemod relies on an external dependency. We have automatically added this dependency to your project's `requirements.txt` file. 

This library holds security tools for protecting Python API calls. 

There are a number of places where Python project dependencies can be expressed, including `setup.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`, and `requirements.txt` files. If this change is incorrect, or if you are using another packaging system such as `poetry`, it may be necessary for you to manually add the dependency to the proper location in your project.

body:
The default `mimetype` for `make_response` in Flask is `'text/html'`. This is true even when the response contains JSON data.
If the JSON contains (unsanitized) user-supplied input, a malicious user may supply HTML code which leaves the application vulnerable to cross-site scripting (XSS). 
This fix explicitly sets the response type to `application/json` when the response body is JSON data to avoid this vulnerability. Our changes look something like this:

```diff
from flask import make_response, Flask
import json

app = Flask(__name__)

@app.route("/test")
def foo(request):
    json_response = json.dumps({ "user_input": request.GET.get("input") })
-   return make_response(json_response)
+   return make_response(json_response, {'Content-Type':'application/json'})
```

body:
Many developers will be surprised to learn that `requests` library calls do not include timeouts by default. This means that an attempted request could hang indefinitely if no connection is established or if no data is received from the server. 

The [requests documentation](https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user/advanced/#timeouts) suggests that most calls should explicitly include a `timeout` parameter. This codemod adds a default timeout value in order to set an upper bound on connection times and ensure that requests connect or fail in a timely manner. This value also ensures the connection will timeout if the server does not respond with data within a reasonable amount of time. 

While timeout values will be application dependent, we believe that this codemod adds a reasonable default that serves as an appropriate ceiling for most situations. 

Our changes look like the following:
```diff
 import requests
 
- requests.get("http://example.com")
+ requests.get("http://example.com", timeout=60)
```

author: pixeebot[bot]
body:
This codemod sandboxes calls to [`requests.get`](https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/#requests.get) to be more resistant to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks.

Most of the time when you make a `GET` request to a URL, you're intending to reference an HTTP endpoint, like an internal microservice. However, URLs can point to local file system files, a Gopher stream in your local network, a JAR file on a remote Internet site, and all kinds of other unexpected and undesirable outcomes. When the URL values are influenced by attackers, they can trick your application into fetching internal resources, running malicious code, or otherwise harming the system.
Consider the following code for a Flask app:

```python
from flask import Flask, request
import requests

app = Flask(__name__)

@app.route("/request-url")
def request_url():
    url = request.args["loc"]
    resp = requests.get(url)
    ...
```

In this case, an attacker could supply a value like `"http://169.254.169.254/user-data/"` and attempt to access user information.

Our changes introduce sandboxing around URL creation that force developers to specify some boundaries on the types of URLs they expect to create:

```diff
  from flask import Flask, request
- import requests
+ from security import safe_requests

  app = Flask(__name__)

  @app.route("/request-url")
  def request_url():
    url = request.args["loc"]
-   resp = requests.get(url)
+   resp = safe_requests.get(url)
    ...
```

This change alone reduces attack surface significantly because the default behavior of `safe_requests.get` raises a `SecurityException` if
a user attempts to access a known infrastructure location, unless specifically disabled.


If you have feedback on this codemod, [please let us know](mailto:feedback@pixee.ai)!

## F.A.Q. 

### Why does this codemod require a Pixee dependency?

We always prefer to use built-in Python functions or one from a well-known and trusted community dependency. However, we cannot find any such control. If you know of one, [please let us know](https://ask.pixee.ai/feedback).

### Why is this codemod marked as Merge After Cursory Review?

By default, the protection only weaves in 2 checks, which we believe will not cause any issues with the vast majority of code:
1. The given URL must be HTTP/HTTPS.
2. The given URL must not point to a "well-known infrastructure target", which includes things like AWS Metadata Service endpoints, and internal routers (e.g., 192.168.1.1) which are common targets of attacks.

However, on rare occasions an application may use a URL protocol like "file://" or "ftp://" in backend or middleware code.

If you want to allow those protocols, change the incoming PR to look more like this and get the best security possible:

```diff
-resp = requests.get(url)
+resp = safe_requests.get(url, allowed_protocols=("ftp",))
```

## Dependency Updates

This codemod relies on an external dependency. We have automatically added this dependency to your project's `requirements.txt` file. 

This library holds security tools for protecting Python API calls. 

There are a number of places where Python project dependencies can be expressed, including `setup.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`, and `requirements.txt` files. If this change is incorrect, or if you are using another packaging system such as `poetry`, it may be necessary for you to manually add the dependency to the proper location in your project.

## 변경사항
- AWS 에서 생성하는 EC2 VM, Snapshot, AMI 에 대한 Tag 를 정리하여, 공통적인 태그를 일관성 있게 적용합니다.
- Builder VM 의 성능사양을 micro 에서 small 로 변경합니다. 2 GiB 의 메모리를 제공하여, mysql, tools container 를 실행을 위한 충분한 메모리를 제공합니다.
- `docker-config.json` 을 git 에서 변경사항 감지를 하지 않도록, 설정을 변경합니다.

author: friofry
body:
## Puzzle-Based Authentication Implemented Argon2-based proof-of-work authentication to protect RPC endpoints. Clients solve ~0.5 second puzzles to get JWT tokens for API access. fixes #49 ### Implementation **New Components:** - `go-auth-service/` - Go microservice for puzzle generation/validation - `test-api/` - React test app with live demo - Nginx Lua integration for token validation (basic auth is still possible) - Grafana metrics integration **Authentication Flow:** ``` 1. GET /auth/puzzle → Challenge + Argon2 params + HMAC 2. Client solves puzzle (find nonce with leading zeros) 3. POST /auth/solve → Submit solution + HMAC verification 4. Receive JWT token (10min expiry, 100 requests) 5. Use token for authenticated RPC calls (cached on nginx side) ``` ### Security Features **Argon2id Algorithm:** - Memory-hard (16MB per attempt) - resists GPU/ASIC attacks - HMAC-protected challenges prevent solution forgery - Configurable difficulty (currently ~256 attempts avg) ### Testing & Demo **Live Demo:** https://rpc-test.callfry.com/ 1. Click "Get Puzzle" 2. Click "Solve Puzzle" 3. Click "Submit Solution & Get Token" 4. Test authenticated requests go solver: [go-auth-service/internal/puzzle/puzzle.go](https://github.com/status-im/eth-rpc-proxy/pull/50/files#diff-2a0b8c2e7a5191754329af13be98c97d060df03a629c6510c6463a46ecbafa5bR93) js solver: [test-api/src/components/PuzzleSolver.js](https://github.com/status-im/eth-rpc-proxy/pull/50/files#diff-2b5cba2b5339824ac30b70db981ec6f778f9ba5729fc70ae6bb13a123cc9f038R109) ### Performance Impact **Client:** One-time 0.5s computation per 10min session **Server:** <1ms puzzle generation, efficient JWT validation (stateless) ### Configuration ```json { "puzzle_difficulty": 1, // Exponential difficulty (2^n * 16 attempts) "requests_per_token": 100, // Rate limit per token "token_expiry_minutes": 10, // JWT lifetime "argon2_params": { "memory_kb": 16384, // 16MB memory requirement "time": 4 // Argon2 iterations "threads": 4, "key_len": 32 } } ``` ### Deployment - New service: `go-auth-service:8081` - Updated nginx with Lua auth middleware - Docker multi-arch builds included - Backwards compatible (optional authentication) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant C as "Client
(Browser/App)" participant N as "Nginx Proxy
:8080" participant A as "Auth Service
:8081" participant R as "RPC Backend
(Infura/etc)" Note over C,R: 🔐 Puzzle-Based Authentication Flow C->>N: Request RPC without token N->>A: auth_request /auth/verify A->>N: ❌ 401 Unauthorized N->>C: ❌ 401 - Auth Required Note over C,A: 🧩 Get Puzzle Challenge C->>A: GET /auth/puzzle A->>A: Generate challenge + salt + HMAC A->>C: Puzzle {challenge, salt, difficulty=1, argon2_params} Note over C: 💻 Solve Puzzle (~0.5s)
Find nonce where
Argon2(challenge+salt+nonce)
starts with "0" (16MB memory) Note over C,A: ✅ Submit Solution C->>A: POST /auth/solve
{nonce, argon_hash, hmac} A->>A: 1. Verify HMAC signature
2. Validate Argon2 computation
3. Check difficulty requirement A->>C: JWT Token (10min, 100 requests) Note over C,R: 🚀 Authenticated RPC Requests C->>N: RPC request + Bearer token N->>A: auth_request /auth/verify A->>A: Validate JWT + rate limits A->>N: ✅ 200 OK (cached in Nginx) N->>R: Forward to RPC backend R->>N: RPC response N->>C: Response Note over C,R: 🔄 Subsequent requests use cached validation ``` ### Metrics ### Alternatives * SHA-256: very easy to parallize without memory penalty * Equihash: overkill complexity for DDoS * More complex Argon2: verification on the server side requires more computation (the same as client) * VDF: Less standard (argon2 algorithm has very good library support) So Argon2 + Leading Zeros: simple implementation + effective DDoS protection

author: copilot
body:
The GitHub Actions workflow was failing because `npm ci` requires a `package-lock.json` file, but it was missing from the repository and explicitly ignored in `.gitignore`.

## Issue
The CI workflow in `.github/workflows/azure-deploy.yml` uses `npm ci` to install dependencies, but failed with:
```
npm error The `npm ci` command can only install with an existing package-lock.json or
npm-shrinkwrap.json with lockfileVersion >= 1. Run an install with npm@5 or
later to generate a package-lock.json file, then try again.
```

## Root Cause
1. `package-lock.json` was missing from the repository
2. The file was explicitly listed in `.gitignore`, preventing it from being tracked

## Solution
- Generated `package-lock.json` by running `npm install` (creates lockfileVersion 3 with 510 packages)
- Removed `package-lock.json` from `.gitignore` to allow the file to be tracked
- Verified `npm ci` now works correctly with the generated lockfile

## Changes
- **Added**: `package-lock.json` (248KB file with exact dependency versions)
- **Modified**: `.gitignore` (removed `package-lock.json` entry)

This ensures reproducible builds and allows the GitHub Actions workflow to install dependencies successfully.

Fixes #1.

**Changes**

This PR allows Windows users to define in the `phpstan.neon` file custom `configDirectories`.

```
parameters:
    configDirectories:
        - config
        - modules/*/Config
```

Before this change only Unix-like system could use this functionality as the absolute path was wrong for Windows users.

Before PR: `C:\Users\User\Herd\laravel\modules/ModuleA/Config/config.php`
After PR: `C:\Users\User\Herd\laravel\modules\ModuleA\Config\config.php`

The `glob` method returns the path following the directory separator in the provided pattern.

Before the PR this condition was always false for Windows users as the path did not match:

https://github.com/larastan/larastan/blob/36706736a0c51d3337478fab9c919d78d2e03404/src/Rules/NoEnvCallsOutsideOfConfigRule.php#L83

author: ludobermejoes
body:
… y estático

Este commit introduce una reestructuración exhaustiva del proceso de compilación para solucionar problemas de enlazado con la librería OpenSSL en diferentes sistemas operativos, mejorando significativamente la fiabilidad de la integración continua (CI) y la experiencia de desarrollo. El cambio principal se encuentra en el workflow de GitHub Actions (`release.yml`), donde se han añadido pasos específicos para cada plataforma. Para Linux, se instalan los paquetes `pkg-config` y `libssl-dev` para asegurar la presencia de las cabeceras de desarrollo de OpenSSL. Para macOS, el workflow ahora intenta instalar `openssl@3` mediante Homebrew y configura las variables de entorno necesarias (`OPENSSL_DIR`, `PKG_CONFIG_PATH`, etc.) para que el compilador de Rust pueda localizar esta versión. Crucialmente, el paso de compilación (`cargo build`) ha sido modificado para implementar un mecanismo de fallback: primero intenta compilar enlazando dinámicamente con la librería OpenSSL del sistema; si falla, reintenta la compilación activando la feature `vendored-openssl`. Esta feature, definida en `Cargo.toml` y que utiliza el crate `openssl-src`, compila OpenSSL desde sus fuentes y la enlaza estáticamente, eliminando dependencias externas. Para soportar esto, se añadió la dependencia `openssl` y se creó el archivo `OPENSSL_SOLUTIONS.md` para documentar posibles soluciones a problemas de compilación locales. Finalmente, se aplicaron cambios de formato menores en varios archivos Rust, sin alterar la lógica.

BREAKING CHANGE: N/A

Test Details: N/A

Security: El commit modifica la gestión de la dependencia criptográfica OpenSSL. Al priorizar el uso de la librería OpenSSL del sistema, existe un riesgo potencial de que la aplicación se enlace dinámicamente con una versión antigua y vulnerable de OpenSSL si no se actualiza en el entorno de compilación. Sin embargo, este riesgo es mitigado significativamente en el entorno de CI por dos factores: el workflow intenta instalar versiones recientes y, más importante aún, el mecanismo de fallback a una versión "vendored" (compilada desde la fuente, OpenSSL v3.5.0) asegura que se utilice una versión moderna y segura si la del sistema falla o es incompatible. Por lo tanto, aunque se interactúa con una dependencia crítica de seguridad, el cambio está diseñado como una medida de robustez y seguridad para el proceso de build, no introduce una vulnerabilidad directa.

author: surajsahani
body:
This feature introduces a real-time display of the number of currently online users.

Key changes:

Backend (`backend/main.py`):
- Added a new API endpoint `/api/online-users`.
- This endpoint queries Firebase Realtime Database (`/status` path) to count users with `online: true`.
- Fixed an initial bug where it counted all users under `/status` instead of only those marked as online.

Frontend (`src/`):
- `contexts/AuthContext.tsx`:
    - Implemented user presence tracking using Firebase Realtime Database.
    - When you log in, your status is set to `{online: true, last_changed: serverTimestamp()}` at `/status/{uid}`.
    - `onDisconnect` handler ensures status is updated to `{online: false, ...}` if you disconnect abruptly.
    - On explicit logout, status is immediately set to `{online: false, ...}`.
- `components/Header.tsx`:
    - Displays the online user count fetched in real-time from the `/status` path in Firebase Realtime Database.
    - Shows a green icon (Signal) and the count (e.g., "186 Online").
    - The display is responsive, showing a compact version on smaller screens.
    - The count is only displayed for logged-in users.

Testing:
- Backend API was tested to ensure correct counting of online users.
- Frontend logic was reviewed for correct presence management and display updates.

Une icône + plus grande est intégrée à gauche du texte pour une meilleure affordance.

body:
Shortcut Story ID: [sc-62150]

Includes https://github.com/RoundingWell/care-ops-frontend/pull/1464

Switches to @cypress/code-coverage

I don't love how `npm test` will reset coverage after any test run in interactive mode "open"
But it's way faster.. and now we can run `npm run coverage` to get a pretty quick full report.. and we _could_ use `describe.only` or `specify.only` with `npm run coverage` if we want a report for specific tests..  _I think_

Anyhow.. it's faster for dev.. it's faster for CI... we don't have to maintain coverage code with other dependency updates.. seems like a win.

author: axelboc
body:
I'll document everything in the Storybook and deal with CSS variables in a separate PR.

A couple of details:

- I move everything that was in the `dimension-mapper` folder in `@h5web/app` to the lib except for:
  - the dimension mapper store (the store that helps us persist the dimension mapping state when inspecting, switching vis, navigating, etc.)
  - the `useValuesInCache` hook, which helps us remove the debounce delay when slicing (when landing on a slice that is already in the cache)

- I move two additional utilities to the lib, which are essential to be able to work with a dimension mapping state: `getSliceSelection` and `useSlicedDimsAndMapping` (again I'll document those in the Storybook in a separate PR).

- From `@h5web/lib`, I expose only the `DimensionMapper`, not the lower-level components (`AxisMapper` and `SlicingSlider`).

author: duyquyen96
body:
Description of the issue/feature this PR addresses:

**Problem:** When archiving channels, statistics (total_slides, total_votes) were reset to 0

When a course (channel) is archived, all its slides are also archived. Since slide statistics 
(total_slides, total_votes, total_views, etc.) are computed based on active and published slides,
archiving caused the computed values to reset to 0. This confused users who expected statistics
to reflect the state of the course before it was archived.

To solve this, we added a new context key: `skip_compute_during_toggle_active`. When toggling
the active state of a channel (i.e., during archive/unarchive), we temporarily disable the
`_compute_slides_statistics` method by checking this context flag. This ensures the statistics
remain intact and reflect their last computed values before archival.

This change improves clarity and preserves the integrity of the statistical data for archived courses.

This is much easier to do than changing the whole data structure to AIG, and should provide similar sharing of key circuits as the AIG encoding does. While this does not provide *full* subcircuit sharing, it shares "enough": It shares the computation of the state vector and the output, which is the key construction that will prevent blowup of the circuit size. 

This is an alternative implementation strategy to #1330 , which requires moving wholesale to AIGs. That's quite a drastic and deep change, and would need more time to be robust.

body:
## Summary

Branching from initial [PR](https://github.com/developmentseed/geozarr-examples/pull/13) from @wietzesuijker🙏🏼, this PR is a WIP for experimenting GeoZarr from EOPF Sentinel-2
For now, it simply adds Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (COG) style multiscale functionality to the geozarr-examples repository, implementing proper overview levels that maintain native projections and follow industry best practices.

## Changes

### 🆕 **New Helper Module**: `src/geozarr_examples/cog_multiscales.py`

A comprehensive utility module providing:
- **COG-style overview calculation** with /2 downsampling logic
- **Native CRS preservation** (no reprojection to Web Mercator)
- **Proper coordinate array generation** for each overview level
- **CRS storage** with multiple format support (WKT, EPSG, PROJ4)
- **Numpy-based downsampling** (no external dependencies)
- **Verification and visualization functions**

### 🔄 **Updated Notebook**: `docs/examples/06_multiscales_as_WebMercatorQuad_EOPFZarrV3.ipynb`

- **Simplified and maintainable** by importing helper functions
- **Focuses on workflow** rather than implementation details
- **Some documentation** with clear examples
- **Demonstrates xarray.plot()** working with proper coordinates

## Key Features

### ✅ **Follows COG Conventions**
- Overviews maintain native projection (UTM in example)
- Uses /2 downsampling logic (1:1, 1:2, 1:4, 1:8, etc.)
- Stops when dimensions < 256 pixels
- Compatible with WebMercatorQuad TMS for serving

### ✅ **Maintains Geospatial Integrity**
- Each overview level has proper x/y coordinate arrays
- Native CRS preserved across all levels
- Proper geotransform information maintained
- CF-compliant metadata and standard names

### ✅ **Modern Implementation**
- Zarr V3 format with efficient compression
- Consolidated metadata for fast access
- Proper chunking for cloud-optimized access
- Works with xarray's native plotting

## Next

- CF conventions translation

I hope this experimental implementation could provides a foundation for COG-style multiscale GeoZarr datasets for EOPF

author: fmount
body:
Starting with `RHOSO 19`, `Nova` and `Cinder` adopt `Glance`'s new `location API`, 
eliminating the need for default splitting. 
This change enables `single` `GlanceAPI` deployments with supported `backends` 
(`S3`, `Ceph`, `Cinder`, `Swift`) for both greenfield and existing environments.

This enables a single Glance  `StatefulSet` deployment with several benefits:

- Reduces `PVC` resource requirements (e.g., halving staging area storage)
- Simplify deployment `topologies` and use cases
- Maintains split model for upgrade compatibility

**Note:** Existing split deployments cannot automatically migrate to single layout. 
A migration procedure is included as part of this patch.

Jira: https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OSPRH-17562

author: nu-wa
body:
Hello,

I encountered an error when trying to enable caching in my project, I could not compile any Plugins due to a bad configuration file used by the wasmtime crate (`failed to parse config file`). I managed to find understand the error after seeing [some changes  made by wasmtime](https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasmtime/pull/10859) and its documentation. I was simply missing the `enabled` key from the configuration, that has been removed from `wasmtime` (and its [cache sister crate](https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasmtime/tree/main/crates/cache)).

So I added more information in the README regarding this specific issue, and some extra behaviour that I noticed would happen regarding caching configuration.

Hopefully this is helpful!

author: leosvelperez
body:
## Current Behavior

Some Angular migrations collect the Angular projects from the project graph using the dependencies information. When reading the project configuration for those projects, it can throw an error if trying to do it for a completely inferred project (it doesn't have a project configuration file).

## Expected Behavior

The Angular migrations collecting Angular projects from the project graph using the dependencies information should gracefully handle projects that were completely inferred when trying to read the project configuration.

In fact, the current migrations didn't need to read the project configuration and could use the project graph information directly, so the call to read the project configuration was removed.

## Related Issue(s)

Fixes #31607

body:
# Ticket

https://community.openproject.org/wp/64636

# What are you trying to accomplish?

Prevent importing the same enterprise token twice.

## Screenshots
<!-- Provide before/after screenshots, videos, or graphs for any visual changes; otherwise, remove this section -->

# What approach did you choose and why?

It's not very strict right now: it relies on rails uniqueness validation. There is no database unique constraint so two parallel requests could add the same token, but that's unlikely to happen.

You can also import the same token twice if you add some garbage before and/or after, but it strips whitespaces and for most customer scenarios, it should be enough as users are unlikely to add random characters before their token.

Also even if the same token is added twice, it's not a big deal. It will still work as expected.

This PR addresses a flaky test `Custom RPC history deletes a custom RPC`. The test occasionally failed due to a race condition where the dropdown is interacted with before the network removal is fully processed in the background. So a background error `network configuration not found` can occur.

author: ahneun-byul
body:
各設定について内容説明
- `semi: false` : 行末のセミコロン省略
> JS/TSではセミコロンがなくても動作し、コードがよりきれいに見える場合があります。 好みの違いですが、最近は省略するスタイルも多いです
- `singleQuote: true` : 文字列にシングルクォーテーションを使用
> ほとんどのJS/TS開発者が好みます。 Vueともよく似合います。
- `printWidth: 100` : 1行最大長さ制限
> 長すぎると可読性が低下し、短すぎると行が多すぎます。 100は適当中間線だと思います。
- `tabWidth: 2` : インデント空白数
> Vueでは通常2マスが標準です。 HTML/CSS/JS 統一性が維持されます。
- `trailingComma: "es5"` : オブジェクト/配列で最後のコンマを許可
> Gitでdiffがきれいで、新しい属性を追加する時に便利です。
- `bracketSpacing: true` : オブジェクトリテラル中括弧に空白を挿入 (`{ a: 1 }`)
> 空白の方が読みやすく、一般的に好まれます。
- `arrowParens: "avoid"` : 矢印関数で因子が 1 つの場合、括弧省略 (`x => x`)
> 短くて簡潔なコード作成に有利です。
- `htmlWhitespaceSensitivity: "ignore"` : HTML/Vueテンプレートの空白感度を低くします。
> Vue `<template>`でレイアウトが壊れないようにするために必要です。
- `vueIndentScriptAndStyle: true` : `<script>`、`<style>`内にもインデント
> Vueで構造的に区分がよくなるように保障されます。

### Description of the change

Minimal changes were made to the Grafana subchart involving the rendering of `{{ .Values.datasources.secretName }}` to both the `deployment.yaml` and the `serviceaccount.yaml`. These changes more closely align with the rest of the chart's capabilities involving templated rendering of value file attributes.

### Benefits

This change is backwards compatible while providing a more customized way of setting the DataSource's secret name in the chart. The templated rendering should still keep the functionality of previous implementation, while providing more needed customization.
This change would allow me to deploy a secret name based on some variables in the chart, instead of the current approach, which only accepts a hardcoded non-templated value.

### Possible drawbacks

In all honesty, I don't think this causes any drawbacks. The changes were minimal to the Grafana chart (2 lines) and they're backwards compatible.

body:
The run-buildbot script with verbose output generates thousands of lines of output about copying headers around. This output makes it very difficult to find the actual CI failures among the noise.

The original idea behind verbose output was that it would help debug CI failures.

I believe the non-verbose CMake output is
(A) Sufficient to debug any issues you encounter, given that the cmake failure and log files are uploaded as artifacts.
(B) It would be much easier to debug CI failures if the logs were shorter.

Verbose output from the buildbot script can still be enabled using `-v` or `--verbose`

author: rwestrel
body:
Patch doesn't apply cleanly: - jdk21u still has IU barriers: context for some of the changes is different. - Because of IU barriers, there's an extra call to `fix_ctrl()` for which the renaming to `nodes_above_barriers` must be applied. - The initial patch makes a subtle change that doesn't affect jdk 25/26 in the code that was refactored. `ShenandoahBarrierC2Support::push_data_inputs_at_control()` is introduced with logic: ``` if (in != nullptr && phase->has_ctrl(in) && phase->get_ctrl(in) == ctrl) { ``` which replaces the same logic in `ShenandoahBarrierC2Support::fix_ctrl()` but also a slightly different logic in `ShenandoahBarrierC2Support::is_dominator_same_ctrl()`: ``` if (m->in(i) != nullptr && phase->ctrl_or_self(m->in(i)) == c) { ``` that is, it uses `ctrl_or_self()` which works for both data nodes and control nodes but the new method uses `has_ctrl(in) && get_ctrl(in)` which can only be true for data nodes. That change causes failures in jdk 21 again because of IU barriers that produce a new memory state when expanded and need the logic from `MemoryGraphFixer`. What I propose in this backport to be on the safe side is to leave `ShenandoahBarrierC2Support::is_dominator_same_ctrl()` alone (not apply that part of the refactoring). Tested with hotspot_gc_shenandoah + tier1 with -XX:+UseShenandoahGC --------- ### Progress - [x] Change must be properly reviewed (1 review required, with at least 1 [Reviewer](https://openjdk.org/bylaws#reviewer)) - [x] [JDK-8358334](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8358334) needs maintainer approval - [x] Change must not contain extraneous whitespace - [x] Commit message must refer to an issue ### Issue * [JDK-8358334](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8358334): C2/Shenandoah: incorrect execution with Unsafe (**Bug** - P2 - Approved) ### Reviewers * [William Kemper](https://openjdk.org/census#wkemper) (@earthling-amzn - Author) Review applies to [25cba14f](https://git.openjdk.org/jdk21u-dev/pull/1901/files/25cba14fc668aca1781f24afb10032121f2f8f94) * [Aleksey Shipilev](https://openjdk.org/census#shade) (@shipilev - **Reviewer**) ### Reviewing

The motivation for this change is prior to Commit 7d3da68f792018e81a758881e081154d1cbe6b6f ("examples : use miniaudio for direct decoding flac, mp3, ogg and wav (#2759)", there was a step that read stereo int16 data -> pcm16 (448512 samples), and then converted to mono (224256 samples), and then also convert to stereo in `pcmf32s`.

The middle step here seems to have been missed when rewriting the code to use Miniaudio and caused issues when transcribing stereo audio files.

For example, currently using the audio sample in the linked issue the output is:
```console
[00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:03.000]  (speaker 1) Sous-titres réalisés para la communauté d'Amara.org
```

And with the change in this commit the output is:
```
[00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:01.500]  (speaker 1) *sonnerie de téléphone*
[00:00:01.500 --> 00:00:07.000]  (speaker 1) Salut jeune homme !
[00:00:07.000 --> 00:00:08.500]  (speaker 0) C'est vrai que je te dérange ?
[00:00:08.500 --> 00:00:10.500]  (speaker 1) Ah pas du tout, pas du tout, pas du tout !
[00:00:10.500 --> 00:00:12.500]  (speaker 1) J'étais en train de...
[00:00:12.500 --> 00:00:14.500]  (speaker 1) de préparer un courrier
```

Resolves: https://github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp/issues/3092

----
Notes/writeup: [diarize-issue](https://github.com/danbev/learning-ai/blob/main/notes/whisper/diarize-issue.md#diarize-issue)

body:
Continuation of https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/127148

When datanodes send the STATS intermediate states to the coordinator, it aggregates them.
Now, however, the TopN groups sent by a datanode may not be acceptable in the coordinator (Because it has better values already), so it will discard such values.

However, the engine wasn't handling intermediate groups with nulls (TopNBlockHash uses nulls to discard unused groups).
See https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/x-pack/plugin/esql/compute/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/compute/aggregation/GroupingAggregator.java#L47

_This code isn't connected with the query yet, so there's no bug in production_

author: galzath
body:
…rontend planning

This commit includes the backend implementation for a new multi-turn conversational flow in Conrad and prepares for frontend integration.

Key changes:

Backend (`conrad_backend`):
1.  **`app/schemas.py`**: Enhanced `ChatResponse` to support new interaction types by adding `clarification_type`, `available_spaces`, and `remaining_topics` fields.
2.  **`app/services/confluence_service.py`**: Added `get_available_spaces()` method to fetch all global Confluence spaces, enabling you to select a search scope.
3.  **`app/core/state_manager.py`**: Upgraded `SessionData` to manage a richer conversational context, including `available_spaces`, `selected_space_key`, and `clarification_type` to track the conversation state across multiple turns.
4.  **`app/main.py`**: Significantly refactored the `/chat` endpoint to orchestrate the new conversational flow:
    *   Initiates interaction by prompting you for Confluence space selection.
    *   Processes your space choice and performs scoped searches.
    *   Handles 'no results' scenarios by offering to broaden the search (e.g., search all spaces, select another space).
    *   Integrates with existing document clarification logic within the selected space.
    *   Sets up the backend to provide 'related topics' (other relevant documents) after an answer is given, especially post-document clarification.
    *   Ensures session context (original question, selections, intermediate results) is maintained throughout the interaction.

Frontend (`popup.js` - Planning & Preparation):
*   Analysis of `popup.js` confirmed its existing clarification UI (`displayClarificationUI`, `handleClarificationSelection`) is largely suitable for handling the new interaction steps (space selection, related topics, broaden search options).
*   The immediate next steps involve modifying `displayDirectAnswer` to show related topics and ensuring the initial message correctly starts the new flow.

This work is part of a larger effort to make Conrad more interactive by guiding you through space selection and offering more options for exploration. The current submission focuses on the backend logic and initial frontend analysis for these features.

author: johnrichardrinehart
body:
<!--
^ Please summarise the changes you have done and explain why they are necessary here ^

For package updates please link to a changelog or describe changes, this helps your fellow maintainers discover breaking updates.
For new packages please briefly describe the package or provide a link to its homepage.
-->

## Things done

I've exposed the `goModules` derivation (generated from the module's `go.mod`/`go.sum`) in `passthru`. I ran into an issue trying to generate derivations for each of the `go` modules in https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-scaffolding-framework/tree/ffe107b9af03f804b72f817502ca45f6b0490fe3 (recent commit on `main`). This repo contains nested `go` modules. So, when performing the `go generate` step in the derivation for `./tools` (cf. [here](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-scaffolding-framework/blob/ffe107b9af03f804b72f817502ca45f6b0490fe3/tools/tools.go#L13-L22)) I found that things were failing because the `vendor` directory in the root didn't match the `go.mod`/`go.sum` associated with the parent module - at least, that's what it looked like. I still need to work to make a reproduction that's not located on my work machine.

I found that by adding a step, where I do something like
```
cp -r ${repoRootDerivation.goModules} ../vendor # ../vendor points to the repo root
```
with the changes from this PR, resolves the `go` compiler's complaints about `modules/vendor.txt` not aligning with `go.mod`/`go.sum`.

I'm posting here right now to gather feedback. But, I plan to share a derivation which uses and benefits from these changes to provide some more concrete technical context. Maybe by looking at the problem this is trying to solve, we can develop a better solution.

I like this solution because it doesn't really change `buildGoModule` (hashes don't change and I didn't need to add a bunch of backward compatibility layers like if I wanted to make `modRoots = [ ./root1 ./sub/root2 ]` and related. This is also a nice change because it allows projects which _don't_ have nested `go` modules to easily inspect the dependencies of a `buildGoModule` derivation by doing something like `nix build ".#${BUILD_GO_MODULE_DRV}.goModules" && tree -L"$BIG_NUMBER" ./result/*`

author: rush86999
body:
This commit introduces a comprehensive setup for deploying your Atomic application stack to AWS using the AWS Cloud Development Kit (CDK).

Key components and features include:

- **CDK Stack (`deployment/aws`):**
  - Provisions core infrastructure: VPC, RDS PostgreSQL, ECS Fargate Cluster, Application Load Balancer, and associated Security Groups.
  - Creates ECR repositories for all custom-built Docker images.
  - Defines ECS Fargate services for: `supertokens`, `graphql-engine`, `functions`, `app`, `handshake`, and `oauth`.
  - Implements path-based routing via the ALB to the respective services.
  - Sets up placeholder secrets in AWS Secrets Manager for sensitive configurations that require manual population post-initial deployment (e.g., database connection strings, Hasura JWT key, external API keys).

- **Deployment Scripts:**
  - `build_scripts/`: Scripts to build individual service Docker images and push them to ECR.
  - `deploy_atomic_aws.sh`: A master script to orchestrate the end-to-end deployment process:
    1. Builds and pushes Docker images.
    2. Deploys the CDK stack.
    3. Executes post-deployment scripts for database initialization and Hasura metadata application.
  - `run_db_init_scripts.sh`: Applies SQL schema files (copied to `db_init_scripts/`) to the RDS instance.
  - `apply_hasura_metadata.sh`: Applies Hasura metadata using the Hasura CLI.

- **Documentation:**
  - `deployment/aws/README.md`: Provides detailed instructions on prerequisites, setup, the deployment process (including the critical step of manually updating placeholder secrets), accessing the application, updating, and troubleshooting.

This initial version provides a "1-script-execution" path to deploy the core services. Further work will be needed to fully automate secret population, integrate additional services from the docker-compose stack (like Optaplanner, Kafka, OpenSearch), and enhance WebSocket support for the ALB.

author: danakj
body:
When resolving a facet type's rewrite constraints, if we find a cycle, we can stop replacing the RHS of constraints. Continuing would only be important if we want to propagate the error through the whole cycle, but once there's an error in a rewrite constraint, the FacetType will also resolve to an error, so there's no benefit to propagating the error more.

Ensure that we still diagnose a conflicting rewrite in the facet type after diagnosing a cycle, in the case that both issues are present in the same facet type.

Together with https://github.com/carbon-language/carbon-lang/pull/5692 this takes our pathological exponential example[1] from running for minutes to running in 17ms, which will still need to be improved by eliminating exponential behaviour. But this avoids wasted work nonetheless.

[1] https://github.com/carbon-language/carbon-lang/pull/5673#discussion_r2152859014

**- What I did**

- related to https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/50066

When an endpoint in a gateway mode "nat" network is selected as a container's default gateway, the bridge driver sets up
bindings between host and container ports (NAT, userland proxy etc).

When gateway mode "routed" was added as an alternative to the default "nat" mode - port bindings followed the same rules. But, unlike "nat" mode, there's no host port binding to set up - there's routing between remote client and the container, so it doesn't matter what the default gateway is.

This new test demonstrates that ports on routed mode endpoints are not accessible all the time - it's split out of https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/50140, which will eventually change the rules for routed mode port publishing.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The `update-cgmanifest.ps1` script was regenerating the entire `cgmanifest.json` file each time it ran, causing the file to show changes in source control even when there were no actual changes to package versions or new packages added.

The script had several issues:
- Package registrations were added in the order they were processed (not alphabetical)
- JSON field ordering was inconsistent between runs
- Even with identical package versions, the file would appear modified in git

## Solution

Modified the script to ensure deterministic, consistent output:

1. **Sort package registrations alphabetically** by package name before writing to JSON
2. **Use ordered hashtables** to ensure consistent field ordering within JSON objects
3. **Maintain consistent JSON structure** across multiple script runs

## Changes Made

- Added sorting of `$newRegistrations` by package name: `$newRegistrations | Sort-Object { $_.component.nuget.name }`
- Implemented ordered hashtables using `[ordered]@{}` syntax to control field ordering
- Ensured consistent structure: `type` before `nuget`, `name` before `version`
- Maintained all existing functionality for package detection and version processing

## Verification

Created comprehensive tests that verify:
- ✅ Multiple script runs produce identical output (zero diff)
- ✅ Packages are sorted alphabetically by name
- ✅ Field ordering is consistent within JSON objects
- ✅ No functional changes to package detection logic

### Example Before/After

**Before:** Running the script twice would show differences like:
```diff
-          "name": "SQLitePCLRaw.bundle_green",
-          "version": "2.1.10"
+          "version": "2.1.10",
+          "name": "SQLitePCLRaw.bundle_green"
```

**After:** Running the script multiple times produces identical output with zero differences.

This resolves the issue where changes to `cgmanifest.json` files would appear in source control unnecessarily, making it easier to identify actual package version changes.

Fixes #30054.

author: gfreitash
body:
Reopening after messing up #288.

## Motivation

The current version detection logic assumes that mods using `automatic-version-check` either:
1. Use GitHub's automatic latest release URL (`releases/latest/download/mod.zip`)
2. Link directly to repository HEAD (`archive/refs/heads/main.zip`)

However, some mod authors, like me, use **permanent release tag URLs** like `releases/download/mod-name__latest/mod.zip` to provide stable download links while still updating the underlying release. This pattern is particularly common in **monorepos** where multiple mods share a single repository.

## Problem

When a mod uses a permanent tag URL, the current script queries the repository's overall latest release, which fundamentally diverge from how releases in a monorepo work. This causes issues where:

- **All mods get the same version**: Every mod gets versioned as whatever release was created most recently across the entire repository
- **False update notifications**: BMM detects "updates" when unrelated mods are released
- **Broken update detection**: Actual updates to specific mods may not be detected

## Solution

This PR adds support for permanent release tag URLs with minimal changes by:

1. **Detecting the pattern**: URLs matching `releases/download/{tag}/{asset}` or `releases/tag/{tag}` (excluding `releases/latest/`)
2. **Querying specific tags**: Instead of `/releases/latest`, query `/releases/tags/{specific-tag}`  
3. **Using asset timestamps**: Generate versions based on the most recent asset's `created_at` timestamp, this avoids generating updates for simple renames in the asset.
4. **Maintaining compatibility**: All existing URL patterns continue to work unchanged

### Key Design Decisions

- **Asset-agnostic**: Uses the most recently created asset instead of searching for specific filenames, keeping it simple and efficient
- **Timestamp-based versioning**: Format `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS` provides human-readable, sequential versions

## Benefits

- **Enables monorepo workflows**: Authors can maintain multiple mods in one repository with reliable update detection by updating specific tags assets
- **Broader ecosystem support**: Works with any permanent tag naming convention
- **Zero breaking changes**: Existing single-mod repositories continue working identically  

## Example

**Before**: All mods in `/balatro-mods` get version `rebalanced-stakes__v1.2.8` (latest across entire repo)

**After**: 
- `qol-bundle` gets version `20240115_103042` (when `qol-bundle__latest` tag has new asset)
- `rebalanced-stakes` gets version `20240116_140521` (when `rebalanced-stakes__latest` tag has new asset)

This enables reliable update detection for each mod independently.

## Considerations
The `update_mod_versions` script currently uses the `created_at` timestamp of the most recent asset to generate versions. This approach is intentionally flexible and works with various ways of updating fixed release tags, but it may be worth considering more opinionated approaches in the future. For example, we could require semantic versioning in release titles or extract changelogs from release bodies, which would open up possibilities for additional features.

This implementation can also be extended to latest-release URLs with little effort, since they just redirect to a specific release tag in the API. Any future metadata extraction features could apply to both URL patterns.

For now, this PR focuses on providing immediate compatibility with minimal friction in the existing environment, while establishing a foundation that can be built upon later.

author: racky124
body:
Overview

This PR introduces the `stack-stream` Clarity smart contract, which enables real-time, continuous streaming of STX and SIP-010 compatible tokens on the Stacks blockchain. The contract allows users to create and manage token streams that disburse tokens based on elapsed time, making it ideal for payroll, subscriptions, vesting, grants, and more.

 Features

- Create a time-based token stream between a sender and a recipient.
- Support for both native STX and SIP-010 tokens.
- Recipient can withdraw tokens in real-time as the stream accrues.
- Ability to cancel a stream and refund unused balance to the sender.
- Read-only functions for retrieving stream metadata and state.

Technical Details

- Language: Clarity
- Contract name: `stack-stream`
- Tested using Clarinet for unit and functional correctness.
- Includes error handling, timestamp validation, and secure token transfer logic.

 Motivation

The contract provides a decentralized solution for programmable money flows, replacing static lump-sum transactions with programmable, streaming payments that improve capital efficiency and user experience.

 Next Steps

- Audit for security vulnerabilities and edge cases.
- Add integration examples for frontend wallets and dashboards.
- Extend support for NFT-based gating or DAO-controlled streams.

author: josejboon
body:
It took a while, but it is finally here... THE CHECKERBOARD PATTERN!!

and.. some norm.. and cleaning... 😅 (it won't happen after this branch!)

Syntax usage: `m_material type:<type> ... pat:<solid|checker>   su:<flt>   sv:<flt>  rot:<flt>  alt_col:<col>`

`pat` is the pattern to be applied onto the object, for default look use solid.
`su` is the scalar for the u axis, and for the checker it means the number of tiles on the horizontal axis.
`sv` is the scalar for the v-axis, and for the checker it means the number of tiles on the vertical axis.
`rot` will rotate the texture coordinates by n degrees, and its value can be between -180.0 and 180.
`alt_col` (maybe rename it to tex_col), is the alternate/ secondary color used for the texture.

The albedo of the material itself also still exists and is used as a tint onto the object color. (Or change this to be the alt_col and remove the alt_col field)?

# Description
## Summary
This PR introduces a new categories application to the project to manage categories functionality. It adds models, views, forms, templates, admin configurations, tests, migrations, and integration with the existing forum app to enable category-dependent features. This includes assigning topics to categories, a category list page, and handling pagination in topics and categories.

### Main Changes:

- New Categories App:  Created categories app with features to:

    * Manage categories in the admin panel
    * Create, edit, and save categories using Django forms
    * Render categories and related topics with templates
    * Use models and migrations to support Category with fields like name, slug, and timestamps

* Forum Integration:

    * Modified the Topic model to include a foreign key to Category
    * Updated forum forms, views, and templates to respect category assignments (e.g., NewTopicForm now includes categories)
    * Added robust test cases for proper category and topic integration

* Testing:

    * Thorough test coverage for categories (models, views, forms, UI/UX, and integration with topics)
    * Pagination, invalid inputs, and UI responsiveness accounted for in both categories and topics

* Miscellaneous:

    * Added beautifulsoup4 as a new dev dependency
    * Updated version in pyproject.toml to 0.2.0 to reflect major functionality addition

This update tightly integrates the feature into the existing setup, ensuring logical association management between categories and forum topics while maintaining robust unit and integration test coverage.

body:
There is a bug in a canonicalization pass in the smt dialect, specifically in the `IteMergePattern`. This code in question claims to do this rewrite: `((x if c else y) if c' else x) -> y if c' && !c else x` (comment on line 259), but instead it actually did this one: `((x if c else y) if c' else x) -> `(x if c' && !c else y)`. 

This has lead to some smt queries giving different results depending on whether canonicalization has been called.
