author: nemo794
body:
### Overview

Currently, `rfiLikelihood` is copied from the input granule to the output QA STATS.h5 file for only RSLC products. However, these `rfiLikelihood` datasets are also in the input GSLC and GCOV products. Based on offline conversations, it would be useful to users to copy this information for GSLC and GCOV as well. This PR implements that feature.


### Implementation

To implement this functionality, the following design choices were made:
* In the product reader, `get_rfi_likelihood_path()` was promoted from the child class `RSLC()` to a parent class `NonInsarProduct`. This allows GSLC and GCOV products to also have access to it. The docstring was updated accordingly.
* A new function `setup_stats_h5_non_insar_products()` was created, which first calls `setup_stats_h5_all_products()`, and then calls the additional setup functions used only by the Non-InSAR products.
    - This allows us to further refactor and reduce copy-paste in the RSLC, GSLC, and GCOV `verify_*` functions. In practice, the `save_nisar_freq_metadata_to_h5()` and `copy_non_insar_imagery_metrics()` functions can be moved from those three `verify_*` functions into one place: the new `setup_stats_h5_non_insar_products()` function.

body:
RoboClerk can now ingest test results and match them up with the tests to make sure all tests have been executed.
The Redmine plugin can now translate from Textile (the markup language used by Redmine) to ASCIIDOC. This improves how redmine ticket contents are rendered in the documentation. Added support for tracking which items are filtered out or ignored based on filter criteria specified in the Redmine Plugin configuration file. These can be added to any document using `@@SLMS:Eliminated()@@`. If you are only interested in certain items, these can be specified using the type parameter e.g. `type=testcase` . 
There is now support for kicking a system level test to the unit test plan (useful when a requirement is difficult to test by a human tester or via the device's user interface)
The plugin interface has been updated to make the plugins more testable.
Better unit testing coverage of the Redmine SLMS plugin

author: martosaur
body:
Changes:
* `LogHog.Context` module allows users to set context that is always exported in `properties`, regardless of how logger metadata is configured. This is useful, because metadata is a free-for-all wildlands: all sorts of things can be inserted it without user knowing about it. So exporting all metadata is almost never a good idea and in order to meaningfully use it users needs to either maintain a list of all metadata keys that they use and are interested in or group all their custom metadata under some non descriptive key like `extra`. The former is inconvenient and the latter results in all metadata nested under single `extra` property. `LogHog.Context.set` sets metadata that will always be exported. The con being, of course, that it's `LogHog` specific and other loggers will most likely ignore it.
* Add `global_context` `LogHog.Config` that is always attached to events. Things like `$lib` and `$lib_version`

author: cloudmark
body:
This PR addresses and fixes several critical bugs within the `<TimeSeries>` component, enabling the correct rendering and dynamic scaling of multi-channel charts, particularly with large datasets. The changes ensure that the component is robust, performant, and behaves as expected when handling complex time series visualizations.

This solves issue [#7789](https://github.com/HumanSignal/label-studio/issues/7789).

### Reason for change

The `<TimeSeries>` component was failing to render data correctly when using a `<MultiChannel>` configuration or the `multiaxis="true"` attribute. The primary symptoms were a blank main chart view despite the overview scrubber being populated, and a Y-axis that would not scale dynamically on zoom.

This was caused by three distinct bugs:
1.  **Rendering Failure:** A typo (`this.line` instead of `channel.line`) in `TimeSeriesVisualizer.jsx` prevented the SVG path for channels from ever being drawn.
2.  **Dynamic Scaling Failure:** The Y-axis scaling logic for large datasets was flawed, using a CSS transform that did not update correctly. The component now forces a proper redraw of the path to ensure the Y-axis scales with the visible data.
3.  **Incorrect Component Invocation:** The `Channel.jsx` component was not correctly activating the `TimeSeriesVisualizer` for multi-channel views, leading to multiple, conflicting chart instances being rendered. The logic is now corrected to render a single, unified visualizer.

### Video

**Before:**
The main chart area is blank and does not render the channel data. The Y-axis is not scaled correctly.

https://www.loom.com/share/50fc240f1bae4d72ad421bdb9c2c8dfa

**After:**
All channels are rendered correctly in a single, unified chart. The Y-axis now scales dynamically and accurately as the user zooms and pans through the data.

https://www.loom.com/share/7d50d09befce4d19ad3da847ca2d6be7

### Rollout strategy

These changes are bug fixes to core functionality and can be rolled out directly. There is no feature flag associated with this fix.

### Testing

Verification was performed by:
1.  Creating a new project with the labeling configuration and task data specified in issue #7789.
2.  Observing the initial broken behavior (no channels rendered).
3.  Applying the code changes and confirming that all channels now render correctly.
4.  Zooming and panning on the timeline to verify that the Y-axis scales dynamically and smoothly as expected.

### Risks

There are no known security or performance risks associated with this change. The fixes improve rendering performance and correctness for the targeted use case. The changes are scoped to the `TimeSeries` component and do not affect other parts of the application.

### Reviewer notes

The core of the fix lies in three places:
-   The typo fix in `TimeSeriesVisualizer.jsx`'s `initializeChannel` method.
-   The updated scaling logic in `TimeSeriesVisualizer.jsx`'s `setChannelRangeWithScaling` method.
-   The corrected component rendering logic in `Channel.jsx`'s `HtxChannelViewD3` function, which now properly uses `TimeSeriesVisualizer` when `multiaxis="true"`.

Please review these three areas to confirm the logic is sound and correctly addresses the issues outlined in the linked ticket.

body:
Custom AI provider management was significantly enhanced to allow in-place editing and multi-preset support.

*   A new `CustomAIProvider` struct (`Models/CustomAIProvider.swift`) was introduced for defining custom provider presets.
*   `CustomAIProviderManager` (`Services/CustomAIProviderManager.swift`), a new singleton, handles CRUD operations, persistence via `UserDefaults`, and selection of these presets. It also migrates legacy single-provider settings.
*   The custom provider UI was refactored into `CustomProviderSettingsView` (`Views/Components/CustomProviderSettingsView.swift`). This view now allows editing the base URL and model without requiring API key deletion, and integrates the new preset selection and management.
*   A dedicated `ProviderPresetEditorView` (`Views/Components/ProviderPresetEditorView.swift`) was created for adding and editing presets.
*   `APIKeyManagementView` (`Views/APIKeyManagementView.swift`) was simplified by replacing its inline custom provider logic with the new `CustomProviderSettingsView`.
*   `VoiceInk.swift` was minimally updated to bind the `CustomAIProviderManager` to the existing `AIService` for application-wide synchronization.

This approach ensures decoupled code and minimal changes to existing files, improving the user experience for managing custom AI providers.

body:
### Description of change

The coverage report is wrong in Codecov, because we don't have `parallel = true`, and we run multiple versions on the same CI worker, so only the latest version of Django that runs is reported.

The project uses `pytest-cov` which does not work with this option:

> This plugin overrides the parallel option of coverage. Unless you also run coverage without pytest-cov it’s pointless to set those options in your .coveragerc.

Dropping this dependency in an attempt to get more accurate combined coverage.

body:
# Add CSVFormatter for YouTube Transcript API

## Summary
This PR adds a new CSVFormatter class to the YouTube Transcript API that outputs transcripts in CSV format with the required columns: `start_time`, `end_time`, `duration`, and `text`.

## Changes Made
- **Created CSVFormatter class** in `formatters.py` that inherits from the base `Formatter` class
- **Implemented required methods**: `format_transcript()` and `format_transcripts()` 
- **Added CSV formatter to FormatterLoader** with key `'csv'`
- **CLI integration**: The `--format csv` option is now available and functional
- **Comprehensive test coverage**: Added tests for basic functionality, multiple transcripts, and special character escaping

## Implementation Details
- Uses Python's built-in `csv` module for proper CSV formatting and escaping
- Calculates `end_time` as `start + duration` following existing patterns
- Uses Unix line endings (`\n`) for consistent output across platforms
- Properly handles special characters (commas, quotes) through CSV escaping
- Follows the same code patterns as existing formatters (JSONFormatter, TextFormatter, etc.)

## CSV Output Format
```csv
start_time,end_time,duration,text
0.0,1.5,1.5,Hello world
1.5,3.0,1.5,"Text with, comma"
3.0,4.0,1.0,"Text with ""quotes"""
```

## Testing
- ✅ All existing tests continue to pass (20/20)
- ✅ New CSV formatter tests pass (3/3)
- ✅ CLI integration verified - `--format csv` option available
- ✅ Special character escaping tested (commas, quotes)
- ✅ Multiple transcript handling tested

## Usage
```bash
# CLI usage
python -m youtube_transcript_api VIDEO_ID --format csv

# Programmatic usage
from youtube_transcript_api.formatters import CSVFormatter
formatter = CSVFormatter()
csv_output = formatter.format_transcript(transcript)
```

Se establece una relación de muchos a muchos (N:N) entre las entidades Panelist y PanelistProperty.

Cambios realizados:
- Se modificó la entidad `Panelist` para incluir una colección de `PanelistProperty` anotada con `@ManyToMany` y `@JoinTable` para definir la tabla intermedia `panelist_panelist_property`.
- Se modificó la entidad `PanelistProperty` para incluir la referencia inversa a la colección de `Panelist` (opcional, pero buena práctica).
- Se actualizó la vista `PanelistsView` para permitir la selección múltiple de `PanelistProperty` al editar un `Panelist`. Esto incluye:
    - Inyección de `PanelistPropertyService`.
    - Adición de un `MultiSelectListBox` al formulario de edición.
    - Lógica para cargar las propiedades existentes del panelista en el `MultiSelectListBox`.
    - Lógica para guardar las propiedades seleccionadas en la relación N:N.
- Se confirmó que `PanelistService` no requiere cambios explícitos debido al uso de JPA y `CascadeType`.
- Se verificó que la configuración `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto = update` se encargará de crear la tabla de unión necesaria.

Esto te permite asignar múltiples propiedades a cada panelista desde la interfaz de edición.

author: bulatgazizov-dev
body:
This PR adds two endpoints.

### Searching courses by user's specified domain, current skill level, and desired skills.

**Request example:**
```
POST /courses/search
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "area": "Python",
  "current_level": "beginner",
  "desired_skills": "FastAPI"
}
```

**Response:** An array of **Course** objects that match the search criteria.

### Get most popular courses.
**Request:**
```
GET /courses/popular
```

**Response:** An array of **Course** objects representing the most popular courses.

### Next steps:

- It is necessary to connect semantic search for searching courses.
- Implement a search for popular courses from the database.

author: chrisflav
body:
We replace the currently existing `CoproductDisjoint` by a predicate for a family of objects, indicating that the pairwise
pullbacks are disjoint and the coproduct inclusions are monomorphisms.

The old predicate is recovered as `BinaryCoproductDisjoint` as an `abbrev`.

We also replace `CoproductsDisjoint` by `CoproductsOfShapeDisjoint` and `BinaryCoproductsDisjoint`. We postpone
the TODO to show that if binary coproducts are disjoint and suitable coproducts exist, then all coproducts of suitable shape are disjoint.

Note that `CoproductDisjoint` changed its meaning, so no deprecation can be added. This should be fine, since it is a leaf file that is hopefully not much used downstream.

author: apostasie
body:
This is part 3 of internal/FS series.

<!> unlike the previous PRs that were essentially consolidation and enforcing atomic writes, this here is more ambitious, and adds net new features (eg: rollbacks and disaster recovery) - as such, it _may_ be more controversial, so, open to discussion here, as usual <!>

This expands on the previous goal (Atomicity and Durability of `WriteFile`) by providing a new version of `WriteFile` that no longer relies on file renames - hence no longer changing inode - making it now 100% compatible with `os.WriteFile` and usable everywhere (including when files are mounted).

Furthermore, it also focuses on enabling _Consistency_, by introducing:
- disaster recovery:
  - if `WriteFile` fails, the file is immediately reverted to its previous version (or removed if it did not exist prior)
  - if `WriteFile` is hard interrupted for any reason, the _next_ `ReadFile` or `WriteFile` call will first revert it to its original content (or remove it if it did not exist)
- rollback: on a successful write, `WriteFileWithRollback` will return a rollback function that can revert changes

`rollback` should be used in the future to ensure higher-level operations _consistency_ and to facilitate cleanup in case of failures. This should make higher-level operations failures able to revert state / cleanup leftover easier.

I do appreciate this is additional complexity, and some of the code is not trivial.
But then:
- the complexity is already here in things like `container.Create` and other places that are manually rollbacking in a baroque / ad-hoc form
- IMHO this is what it takes to implement higher-level consistent data operations

Finally note that this changeset is purely internal to the `filesystem` package and does not change anything in the rest of nerdctl codebase.

Let me know your thoughts overall, and if this is desirable or not.

author: red-portal
body:
Hi All,

I recently realized that the structure up to v0.4 is a bit too rigid to accommodate VI algorithms other than BBVI/ADVI. In particular, algorithms like [Batch and Match](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14758) or [Natural Gradient VI](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.02914) involve specialized parameter update rules that depart from vanilla gradient descent. As such, I am introducing a new layer of indirection: `AbstractAlgorithm`. (In retrospect, I should have listened to @torfjelde when he suggested keeping the `alg` argument that was in v0.2! Sorry!) 

The new interface significantly decouples the top-level entry point `optimize` and the actual implementation. As such, it requires some massive changes to the user-facing interface in v0.4, but I think it's for the better. In particular, each algorithm has to implement the following methods:

```julia
# Initialize the algorithm
function init(rng, alg, q_init) end

# Perform a single step of the algorithm
function step(rng, alg, state, callback, objargs..., kwargs...) end

# Given the final `state`, return/compute an output to the user
function output(alg, state) end
```
(This design was inspired by [ProximalAlgorithms.jl](https://github.com/JuliaFirstOrder/ProximalAlgorithms.jl).)
Now, algorithms that don't rely on SGD-type updates can directly define `step`.

The previous gradient-descent implementation that was in `optimize` is now moved as specializations for the subtype:
```julia
struct ParamSpaceSGD <: AbstractAlgorithm
    problem
    objective
    adtype
    optimizer
    averager
    operator
end
```
which abstracts all gradient-descent-based VI algorithms.  As before, each `objective` type should implement interfaces specific to `ParamSpaceSGD`, like `estimate_objective` or `estimate_gradient`.

An upside of this design is that we can now bundle different design elements into a single algorithm constructor as follows:
```julia
function BBVIRepGrad(
    problem,
    adtype::ADTypes.AbstractADType;
    entropy::Union{<:ClosedFormEntropy,<:StickingTheLandingEntropy,<:MonteCarloEntropy}=ClosedFormEntropy(),
    optimizer::Optimisers.AbstractRule=DoWG(),
    n_samples::Int=1,
    averager::AbstractAverager=PolynomialAveraging(),
    operator::Union{<:IdentityOperator,<:ClipScale}=ClipScale(),
)
    objective = RepGradELBO(n_samples; entropy=entropy)
    return ParamSpaceSGD(problem, objective, adtype, optimizer, averager, operator)
end
```
Within the constructor, we can elegantly check whether the design components are compatible.
Furthermore, it significantly simplifies the user-facing interface:

```julia
T = 1000
alg = BBVIRepGrad(model, adtype; optimizer=Descent(η))
q = q_meanfield_gaussian(model)
q_out, info, state = optimize(alg, T, q)
```
Progress:
* [x] Code
* [x] Tests
* [x] Docstrings
* [x]  Documentation

Some things to discuss:
* I find it unreasonable to put all of the abstract type definitions in `src/AdvancedVI.jl`. Therefore, the abstract type definitions are a bit scattered depending on the level of the type hierarchy. For example, types belonging to `ParamSpaceSGD` are now in `src/paramspacesgd/abstractobjective.jl`. However, I am not sure if this is optimal.
* At the same time, I wonder if subdirectories like `src/paramspacesgd/` should be modularized into their own `module` given that it has its own set of interfaces and abstract types.
* The algorithms now need a more specific name. For example, ELBO maximization with SGD and the reparametrization gradient needs to be called something. Right now, I am using `BBVIRepGrad`, but not sure if this is the best name. `ADVI` is a more classic choice. But personally, I am not entirely satisfied with either `BBVI` or `ADVI` since it doesn't convey the fact that these algorithms are maximizing the ELBO using stochastic gradient descent in the space of parameters :shrug: . 

Any feedback on the styling or organization is much welcome!

body:
This commit addresses your feedback on the initial TensorChunk serialization refactoring. It includes enhanced test coverage and refined code comments for improved clarity and robustness.

Key improvements:

1.  **Enhanced Test Coverage (`serializable_tensor_unittest.py`):**
    *   I added new test cases to `SerializableTensorChunk.try_parse` to
        specifically validate:
        *   Handling of `torch.dtype`s not supported by the internal
            NumPy dtype conversion map (ensuring appropriate error
            logging and `None` return).
        *   Handling of malformed `data_bytes` where the byte string
            length is not a multiple of the dtype's item size (ensuring
            error logging and `None` return).
    *   The focused test suite now has 58 passing tests (3 skipped for
        unavailable hardware), up from 56.

2.  **Refined Code Comments:**
    *   I conducted a thorough review of comments in both
        `tsercom/tensor/serialization/serializable_tensor.py` and
        `tsercom/tensor/serialization/serializable_tensor_unittest.py`.
    *   I removed comments that merely described "what" the code does when
        it was self-evident.
    *   I eliminated meta-comments related to development history and
        commented-out code.
    *   I ensured remaining comments and docstrings focus on the "why"
        behind non-obvious logic, important assumptions, or specific
        design choices, adhering to the project's commenting standards.

3.  **Static Analysis and Formatting:**
    *   The code has been re-formatted using Black.
    *   Ruff, MyPy, and Pylint checks pass, with Pylint achieving a
        10/10 score on the main serialization class.

These changes further solidify the Phase 1 refactoring of the tensor transport mechanism.

# nf-core/modules pull request

Many thanks for contributing to nf-core/modules!

Remember that PRs should be made against the master branch.

Learn more about contributing: [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nf-core/modules/tree/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md)
-->

- [ ] If you've added a new tool - have you followed the module conventions in the [contribution docs](https://github.com/nf-core/modules/tree/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md)

    - [ ] `nf-core modules test <MODULE> --profile singularity`

author: steveny91
body:
### What does this PR do?
Previously, when performing queue discovery, if an error occurred while inquiring a specific queue (such as a 2101 "object damaged" or a 2035 "permission denied" error), the entire discovery process would fail and return no queues. This meant that if even one out of 100 queues had an issue, we would miss data for all queues, not just the problematic one. This limitation was due to IBM MQ returning an error code when attempting to inquire a queue with issues, which would halt the discovery process.

This PR changes:
- We now first retrieve all queue names using a metadata query (MQCMD_INQUIRE_Q_NAMES), which does not throw exceptions for problematic queues.
- We then iterate over each queue name and inquire them individually. If a specific queue has an issue, we catch the error, emit a dedicated metric with the error code and error name, and continue processing the remaining queues.

This approach may have a slightly higher resource cost, but it ensures that issues with individual queues do not prevent discovery and monitoring of healthy queues.

Additionally, this PR introduces a new metric (ibm_mq.queue.discovery.error) that tracks problematic queues, including the specific error code and error name as tags. This provides better visibility into which queues are experiencing issues and why, without impacting the monitoring of other queues.

author: krasznaa
body:
Time to ruffle up some feathers...

Triggered by @beomki-yeo's initiative to introduce non-constant magnetic fields in #1017, in which he started migrating the CUDA algorithms to the setup that I made for the host and SYCL algorithms already, I thought we could do this migration first. Before adding the inhomogeneous magnetic field support.

With the idea being that adding support for such magnetic fields should become a fair bit simpler at that point. :thinking:

Now... The Alpaka (CUDA) build was not super optimised so far either. It built the track fitting and finding algorithms as single source files. (Even though the track finding kernel functors were separated into a number of header files.) So, using the SYCL code's setup for the Alpaka library is sort of a worst case scenario for making the build as slow as it can be.

And how slow is it? On my Threadripper I can build just the `traccc::cuda` library in its current setup in a little over a minute.

```
[bash][Legolas]:traccc > cmake --build build-cuda/ --target traccc_core
[262/262] Creating library symlink lib/libtraccc_core.so.0 lib/libtraccc_core.so
[bash][Legolas]:traccc > cmake --build build-cuda/ --target vecmem_cuda
[12/12] Creating library symlink lib/libvecmem_cuda.so.1 lib/libvecmem_cuda.so
[bash][Legolas]:traccc > time cmake --build build-cuda/ --target traccc_cuda
[44/44] Creating library symlink lib/libtraccc_cuda.so.0 lib/libtraccc_cuda.so

real    1m7.819s
user    5m53.934s
sys     1m1.241s
[bash][Legolas]:traccc >
```

(The first two build commands are meant to make sure that only the build of `traccc::cuda` is timed.)

Building `traccc::alpaka` from this branch is on the other hand:

```
[bash][Legolas]:traccc > cmake --build build-alpaka/ --target traccc_core
[262/262] Creating library symlink lib/libtraccc_core.so.0 lib/libtraccc_core.so
[bash][Legolas]:traccc > cmake --build build-alpaka/ --target vecmem_cuda
[12/12] Creating library symlink lib/libvecmem_cuda.so.1 lib/libvecmem_cuda.so
[bash][Legolas]:traccc > time cmake --build build-alpaka/ --target traccc_alpaka
[20/20] Creating library symlink lib/libtraccc_alpaka.so.0 lib/libtraccc_alpaka.so

real    1m48.553s
user    6m2.973s
sys     1m0.067s
[bash][Legolas]:traccc >
```

So yes, not insignificantly longer. I even tried with just 16 threads, which would be more representative of how most people work with the code. The difference is pretty much the same. Since these builds are really dominated by a few long-running processes. (So the slow-down at 16 threads instead of 64 is just ~10 seconds with both builds.)

Still... Once/if this PR is agreed upon, I'll also make a PR redesigning the CUDA algorithms into this setup. Ruffling even more feathers...

Pinging @StewMH and @CrossR for their inputs. (I couldn't list you guys as reviewers...)

author: cconlon
body:
# Description

PR https://github.com/wolfSSL/wolfssl/pull/8867 added use of `getpid()`, and also adjusted the definition of `WC_RNG` in `wolfssl/wolfcrypt/random.h` based on `HAVE_PID`:

```
#if defined(HAVE_GETPID) && !defined(WOLFSSL_NO_GETPID)
    pid_t pid;
#endif
```

The `HAVE_GETPID` define was not being stored to `wolfssl/options.h`, so applications depending on the `sizeof(WC_RNG)` would have gotten a different structure size.

This PR modifies `configure.ac` to define `HAVE_GETPID` in `wolfssl/options.h` if `getpid()` is detected.

# Testing

Existing unit tests, and wolfcrypt-jni test cases.

# Checklist

 - [ ] added tests
 - [ ] updated/added doxygen
 - [ ] updated appropriate READMEs
 - [ ] Updated manual and documentation

## What does this PR do?

### High-Level Design
This pull request introduces a new training script for reinforcement learning (`RL`) with the Qwen2.5-7B model, adds functionality for merging responses in datasets, and updates configuration options for reward models. Below are the most important changes grouped by theme:

### New Training Script for RL
* Added a comprehensive script (`scripts/train/example_singlenode_rl_qwen7b_base_t.sh`) to train 7B model on *single node*. 

### Dataset Response Merging
* Introduced utility functions in `verl/trainer/main_generation.py` for merging responses in datasets (`merge_responses`, `extract_content`, and `merge_aime_responses`). These functions handle dataset formats and group responses by prompt content, ensuring compatibility with both pandas and polars DataFrames.
* Enhanced the `main_task` function to detect AIME datasets and apply the new merging logic. Merged datasets are saved in both Parquet and JSON formats, including additional metadata like prompt content and responses. 

### Reward Model Configuration
* Added a new configuration option `launch_reward_fn_async` to the `dapo_trainer.yaml` file. This enables asynchronous execution of custom reward functions on the CPU during log probability calculations.

author: presiyan-peev
body:
Pull Request: Fix Focus Management for Nested Fields in Lists
🐛 Problem
The PreskoForm's first-error focus management feature was not working correctly for nested fields within list items. While the system properly focused simple fields (like "Event Name"), it failed to focus nested fields (like "Full Name" in a contacts array), leaving users confused when form submission failed without any visible indication of the error location.
🔍 Root Cause Analysis
Through debugging, I identified two separate bugs in the focus management logic:
Bug 1: Incorrect List Field Iteration Logic
The fieldsToIterate array was only adding list containers ('contacts') instead of individual list item fields ('contacts[0].name', 'contacts[0].email', etc.). This was due to incorrect if/else condition ordering where field.propertyName was checked before field.type === "list".
Bug 2: Vue Computed Ref Access Issue
The focus logic was trying to access preskoItemInstance.interactiveElement directly, but interactiveElement is a Vue computed ref that requires .value to access the actual DOM element.
✅ Solution
Fix 1: Reordered Field Processing Logic
Apply to PreskoForm.s...
Fix 2: Proper Vue Computed Ref Access
Apply to PreskoForm.s...
Fix 3: Consistent Scroll Target Behavior
Updated the scroll logic to consistently target the input element (where focus will be placed) rather than inconsistently targeting different elements between simple and nested fields.
🧪 Testing
✅ All existing focus management tests pass
✅ Added comprehensive test coverage for nested field focus behavior
✅ Verified compatibility with simple fields, custom scroll callbacks, and ARIA announcements
✅ Confirmed proper submit:reject event emission with correct firstInvalidPath and firstInvalidEl
📋 PRD Compliance
This fix ensures full compliance with the Focus Management PRD requirements:
F-1: Auto-focus on error (with opt-out support)
F-2: Custom scroll callback support
F-3: DOM identification via data-pk-field attributes
F-4: Default smooth scroll and focus behavior
F-5: Proper event payload emission
F-6: ARIA live-region announcements
🎯 Impact
User Experience: Users now receive clear visual feedback when nested field validation fails
Accessibility: Screen readers properly announce focus changes for nested fields
Developer Experience: Consistent behavior across all field types
Backward Compatibility: No breaking changes; all existing functionality preserved
🔄 Before/After
Before: Form submission with invalid contacts[0].name → No focus, user confused
After: Form submission with invalid contacts[0].name → Smooth scroll and focus to the invalid field
This fix resolves the core issue where users would submit forms with invalid nested data and receive no visual indication of where the validation errors occurred, significantly improving the form user experience for complex, nested form structures.

author: t2gran
body:
### Summary

After #6653 the modes mapping in the Transmodel API is not working correct. The case is that the request is updated using multiple sub-request builders. These builders will copy the request state when created, and when build they will write bask any changes. If two bilders are created with the same scope (or overlapping scope) the builder written back last will overwrite the previous one.

I have fixed this by cleaning up the code and made sure the only one builder is in scope at all times - then it becomes impossible to change two builders.

I have added tests for the mapping code involved and some test on ToString() methods I have changed.

I have changed the `toString()` objects for some of the "embedded" request objects. There is not need to print the type 
for these objects. They are indeed ValueObjects, but some of them are complex to using the convention "field-name : value" is kept. I changed the parentheses to '(' and ')' instead of '{' and '}'. This is done if the `ToStringBuilder.ofEmbedded()` is used. It look like this:

```
RouteRequest{..., journey: (transit: (filters: [(select: [(transportModes: NOT [CABLE_CAR, CARPOOL])])], ..}
```


### Issue

🟥  I have not created an issue for this. This issue where detected at Entur yesterday.


### Unit tests

✅  Unit tests are updated.


### Documentation

✅  JavaDoc is updated.


### Changelog

This is a fix for a PR in the same release, hence should not be in the changelog.


### Bumping the serialization version id

Not needed, I have changed the `toString()` methods of some of the Request objects, no other changes.

body:
Adds to the new `wow_indicators` table we created for area alerts to incorporate all the indicators for building alert emails. With this change now all email indicator data is pre-calculated for the necessary date ranges. This allows for a new building alert data API that takes a list of one or more BBLs and returns all the indicator data for the week and month values, so now there is only a single API request per building alert email rather than a weekly and monthly request for each building and each requires a lot of calculation on the DB, which does not scale well and has made the email sending process extremely slow and taxing for the DB. 

Companion PR to update the building alert email sending process/template: https://github.com/JustFixNYC/auth-provider/pull/101

[sc-16443]

> To publish a pre-release version, pass the --pre-release flag to the vsce package or vsce publish commands:
> 
> vsce package --pre-release
> vsce publish --pre-release
> 
> We only support major.minor.patch for extension versions, semver pre-release tags are not supported. Versions must be different between pre-release and regular releases. That is, if 1.2.3 is uploaded as a pre-release, the next regular release must be uploaded with a distinct version, such as 1.2.4. Full semver support will be available in the future.
> 
> VS Code will automatically update extensions to the highest version available, so even if a user opted-into a pre-release version and there is an extension release with a higher version, the user will be updated to the released version. So, we recommend that extensions use major.EVEN_NUMBER.patch for release versions and major.ODD_NUMBER.patch for pre-release versions. For example: 0.2.* for release and 0.3.* for pre-release.
> 
> If extension authors do not want their pre-release users to be updated to the release version, we recommend always incrementing and publishing a new pre-release version before publishing a release version to make sure that the pre-release version is always higher. Note that while pre-release users will be updated to a release version if it is higher, they still remain eligible to automatically update to future pre-releases with higher version numbers than the release version.
> 
> Pre-release extensions are supported after VS Code version 1.63.0, so all pre-release extensions should have the engines.vscode value in their package.json set to >= 1.63.0.

[Source](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/working-with-extensions/publishing-extension#prerelease-extensions)

author: tgvashworth
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes an issue where linked fighters (like pets, exotic beasts, or vehicles) were being duplicated when cloning lists.

## Problem

When cloning a list that contains equipment with linked fighters:
- The linked fighters were being cloned as regular fighters
- Then the equipment assignment cloning would create them again
- This resulted in duplicate linked fighters in the cloned list

## Solution

Modified the `List.clone()` method to:
- Skip cloning fighters that have a `linked_fighter` relationship
- These linked fighters are automatically created when equipment assignments are cloned

## Testing

Added comprehensive tests to verify:
- List cloning with linked fighters works correctly
- Fighter cloning with linked equipment works correctly
- No duplicate fighters are created
- Costs are calculated correctly

Fixes #322

author: yuanyao-nv
body:
Fixes issue in torch-onnx exporter for Attention: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/156105

Previously the number of heads attributes inferred by the exporter is incorrect. It should be read from input dimension -3 not dimension 3:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26f10e15-bc98-42ac-807a-2e089a7d996a)

But in fact, [torch sdpa](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention.html) doesn't support combined num_heads and head_size dimensions like [ONNX](https://onnx.ai/onnx/operators/onnx__Attention.html) does, so this num_heads attribute is not needed.

Extending support to rank>4 can be left as future work if there is use case for that. The translation logic will look like: Reshape(Q,K,V to 4d) -> Attention -> Reshape(Y to original rank).

cc @justinchuby
